mcqs.question: In physics, work is defined as which of the following?

options.A: Force applied without causing any displacement
options.B: Force multiplied by the displacement in the direction of the force

mcqs.answer: Force multiplied by the displacement in the direction of the force
mcqs.explanation: Work is the product of the component of force in the direction of displacement and the magnitude of that displacement (W = F·s). Option B captures this definition. Option A omits displacement, C describes energy, and D describes power, not work.

mcqs.question: A person pushes a box across a floor with a constant force of 10 N and moves it 5 m in the direction of the push. Which pair correctly represents the force and the displacement?
mcqs.explanation: The applied force is 10 N and the box moves 5 m in the same direction, so the correct pair is given in option C. Options A and B misrepresent either force or displacement, and D mixes units incorrectly.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: Work is done on an object only when which condition(s) are satisfied?

options.A: A force is applied and there is displacement in the direction of the force
options.B: Any force is applied, regardless of motion
options.C: Displacement occurs even if the force is perpendicular to the motion
options.D: A force is applied but the object remains at rest

mcqs.answer: A force is applied and there is displacement in the direction of the force
mcqs.explanation: Work requires a component of force along the direction of displacement. Option A states this correctly. Option B ignores displacement, C describes a case where no work is done, and D has zero displacement, so no work is done.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question: A constant horizontal force of 20 N pushes an object 3 m along the direction of the force. What is the work done on the object?
mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × displacement = 20 N × 3 m = 60 N·m = 60 J. Option A is correct. The other values result from incorrect multiplication or unit errors.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following quantities is expressed in joules (J)?
mcqs.explanation: One joule equals one newton‑meter, which is also kg·m²/s². Option C matches this unit. Option A is a force (newtons), B is speed, and D is power (watts).

mcqs.question: A student lifts a 1.5 kg textbook onto a shelf 2.0 m high. Assuming the upward force equals the weight of the book (≈15 N), how much work does the student do on the book?
mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × displacement = 15 N × 2.0 m = 30 J. The force is applied in the same direction as the displacement, so option A is correct. Options B, C, and D are miscalculations.

mcqs.question: A person carries a bag while walking horizontally across a room. They claim that no work is done because the bag does not move. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: The force on the bag is zero, so no work can be done
options.B: The displacement of the bag is zero, so no work can be done
options.C: The force and displacement are perpendicular, so work is zero
options.D: Work is done because the bag is displaced in the direction of the applied force

mcqs.answer: Work is done because the bag is displaced in the direction of the applied force
mcqs.explanation: When the person carries the bag, the bag moves horizontally with the person while the upward force (supporting its weight) acts vertically. The horizontal displacement together with the horizontal component of the applied force results in work. Option D captures the correct reasoning. Options A, B, and C misinterpret the situation.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: A horizontal force of 10 N is applied to a crate that is lifted vertically upward 2 m by a pulley system. Is work done by the applied horizontal force on the crate?

options.A: Yes, because the crate moves 2 m
options.B: No, because the displacement is perpendicular to the applied force
options.C: Yes, and the work equals 20 J
options.D: No, because the force is not applied in the direction of motion

mcqs.answer: No, because the displacement is perpendicular to the applied force
mcqs.explanation: Work is zero when the displacement is perpendicular to the direction of the applied force. Here the force is horizontal while the crate moves vertically, so the dot product is zero. Option B correctly states this. Option A ignores direction, C incorrectly calculates work, and D repeats the correct reasoning but is phrased as a statement rather than the direct answer; B is the precise answer required.
